India's bowling response was spearheaded by Mohammed Shami (4/81), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 235/10 (73.1 ov), New Zealand's innings completed the first-innings exchange (7 Runs (India)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 55 from TA Blundell, complemented by a commanding 103-run stand between Tom Latham and TA Blundell that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.65 RPO. Jasprit Bumrah (2/39) maintained tight lines for India, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 132/3 (35.7 ov), New Zealand successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Hagley Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 242/10 (62.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 235/10 (73.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 5-Wicket Spell: Trent Boult (5/28), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, KA Jamieson delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (49 Runs & 5 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 54%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, India faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by Trent Boult (1 Runs & 7 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by 7 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While India produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
